text:
Sofia: Quick update — vendor pushed a critical kernel backport for our EU inference hosts. We need to move the EU maintenance slot up by 1 hour today to apply it before peak traffic.

Alex: Ack. What's the new window and estimated impact?

Sofia: New window 18:00-19:00 UTC (was 19:00-20:30). Impact: rolling drain of 2 racks in eu-west1, expected 3–6% request routing increase to other regions for ~20m during each rack drain. SLA should remain met but customers on reserved Dedicated may see brief tail-latency blips.

Incident-Bot: Scheduled maintenance created: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/1723456789-maint (auto-note: customers will receive email at T-2h unless suppressed).

Jules: I'll queue the customer notification. Do we have a short template we can send to Dedicated customers who self-host or use VPC?

Sofia: Yes — here's the short status page blurb and a Dedicated-specific note. Please use both channels (status + email).

Taylor: Can we avoid shifting the public maintenance note again? engineering wants a single patch window to reduce churn.

Sofia: Agreed. This is a one-time advance (we couldn't get the vendor build into our original slot). Posting now to minimize repeated comms.

Alex: Oncall handoff: I can take the active pager for the window and the immediate 1h post-window monitoring. Ravi can be backup for kernel-level issues.

Ravi: I'll be on standby. If the kernel causes a node to fail to boot we should follow the boot-rescue playbook: `docs/playbooks/boot-rescue.md` — I'll be present at T-30.

Sofia: Ops runbook snippet we're using during drains: 
```
1) Drain node: `kubectl drain node-<id> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
2) Apply kernel package: `dpkg -i /tmp/redwood-kernel-patch.deb`
3) Reboot and healthcheck: `./scripts/check-instance-health.sh node-<id>`
```

Alex: Noting routing policy: traffic will route to eu-west2 then us-west1. We'll keep a 5% capacity buffer in eu-west2 to reduce cross-region latency spikes.

Jules: Drafting customer email now. Putting the Dedicated insert below — please tweak tone if too technical.

Jules: `Customer email (Dedicated customers):
Subject: Brief maintenance affecting EU inference capacity — [Action: None required]
Hi —
We're planning a short maintenance today to apply a critical security patch to our EU inference hosts. The window is 18:00–19:00 UTC. During this time, your requests may be routed to adjacent regions for very brief periods, which can introduce minor latency increases for at most ~30 minutes. No action is required on your side. If you have strict region-only routing requirements, reply and we'll arrange a coordinated maintenance or an isolated reserved window.
Thanks,
Redwood Inference Ops
`

Sofia: Also posting this on the status page. Draft status page entry: 
```
Title: Short EU capacity maintenance (kernel security patch)
Start: 18:00 UTC
End: 19:00 UTC
Impact: Rolling reboots of a subset of EU inference hosts. Short, temporary routing to other regions; no expected data loss.
Updates: We'll post progress updates here and notify when complete.
```

Alex: I'll publish the status page entry at T-60 and send the customer email T-120 as Incident-Bot suggested.

Incident-Bot: Status page entry published by Alex — https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/1723456789-maint (auto: email queued for T-120).

Ravi: Quick ops checklist for the window (for whoever is running the drain): 
- Ensure `kv-cache` pods stay warm; don't evict if above 30% cache hit.
- If a node fails to rejoin in 10m, escalate to SRE channel and mark `degraded-routing` in status update.
- If more than 1 rack fails concurrently, execute rollback: stop further drains, revert `traffic-weight` to 100% local, and engage infra oncall.

Taylor: Any customers on Dedicated reserved capacity with strict SLAs? We should pre-call any that might be affected.

Jules: There's a small list of 4 customers with region-only SLA in eu-west1; I'll ring them now and add captions to the email for their POCs.

Sofia: Final note for the handoff template — use this short internal blurb for the person taking the pager: 
```
Handoff template:
- Window: 18:00–19:00 UTC
- Primary: Alex (pager)
- Backup: Ravi
- Expected impact: short routing to other regions, potential tail latency spikes for ~30m
- Status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/1723456789-maint
- Escalation: if reboot fails, @oncall-sre and #eng-sre on Slack; mark status `degraded-routing`
```

Alex: Got it. I'll post this handoff template into the ops notes channel at T-15.

Incident-Bot: Reminder scheduled: handoff reminder at T-15 (15 minutes before maintenance).

Sofia: After the window we'll run a brief reconciliation: confirm model latency with the perf smoke test and post `complete` with the short postmortem notes if we observe anomalies.

Ravi: Agree. I'll run `scripts/perf-smoke --region eu-west1 --models default` at T+10m and paste results into the status update.

Jules: Customer calls done — 3 acknowledged, 1 requested an isolated window; created a follow-up ticket with SEs.

Alex: Post-window update plan: 
- T+0min: update status page to "Verification in progress"
- T+10m: paste perf-smoke results
- T+30m: update to "Completed" with notes and any follow-ups

Sofia: Thanks everyone. Posting final status and customer email now. Leave this thread open for live updates during the window.

Alex: Beginning drains in 5. Will post progress logs here.

Alex: Drain started on rack euw-3a — `kubectl drain` returning graceful requeues.

Alex: Rebooted nodes in euw-3a, healthchecks passing.

Alex: Moving to rack euw-3b.

Incident-Bot: Maintenance progress: 50% complete (1 of 2 racks finished).

Alex: Completed euw-3b, all nodes healthy. Starting perf smoke.

Ravi: Perf smoke results: median latency +7ms, p95 +65ms — within tolerance but flagged for monitoring. Pasted logs to ops storage: `s3://redwood-ops/maintenance/1723456789/perf.log`.

Alex: Updating status page to "Verification in progress" and will set to "Completed" in 30m unless anomalies occur.

Incident-Bot: Maintenance completed — status set to Verification in progress by Alex.

Sofia: Posting final completion note: patch applied, rolling reboots done, no customer-facing incidents. Closing the maintenance.

Alex: Status page updated to Completed. Thanks team.

Jules: Sent final wrap email to Dedicated customers and flagged the one that requested isolation for follow-up.

Sofia: Great work. Will file a short maintenance note in the ops repo and attach the perf log.

Taylor: Thx all — nice and smooth.
